title: Inner relaxation run
statement: Let $K_0,B,P$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{orc}:\{0,1,2,3\}\times\{0,1\}^*\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ be an oracle, let $x$ be a finite Boolean string, and let $\varphi$ be a Boolean. For every $u,j\in\mathbb N$, state $S=(N,L_g,s,s_1,X,w,K,B_s,U,V,T,T_2,Z,C,ch,c,c_1)$, and memory $M:\mathbb Z\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, suppose $K-V=j$, $V\le K$, $U=u<K$, $T=T_2=Z=0$, $ch\le1$, every coordinate of $S$ is at most $B$, and $B_s+K\le B$, $B_s+K\le P$, and $K+1\le B$. Then there are a memory $M'$ and $ch'\in\mathbb N$ such that the machine $A(K_0)$, on input $x$ with oracle $\mathrm{orc}$, runs from state $S$, memory $M$, head position $0$, and label corresponding to reading the mark of $V$ in the relaxation round for $\varphi$, to the state obtained from $S$ by setting $V=0$ and $ch=ch'$, memory $M'$, head position $0$, and label corresponding to incrementing $U$ in that round. Every configuration before the endpoint has all register values at most $B$ and memory head position between $0$ and $P$. Moreover, $M'$ extends the marked positions of $M$ and agrees with $M$ outside the cells $B_s+v$ for $v<K$, while $ch'\le1$. For every $v<K$, if $M'$ marks $B_s+v$, then either $M$ already marks that cell or $\mathrm{orc}$ accepts the encoded query for $(x,\rho,u,v)$, where $\rho=s_1$ if $\varphi$ is true and $\rho=s$ otherwise; conversely, if $V\le v<K$ and that query is accepted, then $M'$ marks $B_s+v$. If $M'=M$, then $ch'=ch$; if $M'\ne M$, then $ch'=1$.

replaced:
Let $K_0,B,P$ be natural numbers, let $\mathrm{orc}$ be a Boolean oracle on four indices
and bit strings, let $x$ be a bit string, let $\varphi$ be a Boolean, and let $u,j$ be
natural numbers. Consider a register state $S$ with coordinates
$N,\mathrm{Lg},s,s_1,X,w,K,B_s,U,V,T,T_2,Z,C,ch,c,c_1$, and a memory $M:\mathbb
Z\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$. Suppose $K-V=j$, $V\le K$, $U=u<K$, $T=T_2=Z=0$,
$ch\le1$, every coordinate of $S$ is at most $B$, $B_s+K\le B$, $B_s+K\le P$, and
$K+1\le B$. Then there are a memory $M'$ and a natural number $ch'$ such that the
program $A(K_0)$, with oracle $\mathrm{orc}$ and input $x$, runs from label
$\mathrm{rlV}(\varphi)$ with state $S$, memory $M$, and head position $0$ to label
$\mathrm{rlNU}(\varphi)$ with the same state except that $V=0$ and $ch=ch'$, memory
$M'$, and head position $0$; at every earlier step, all register values are at most $B$
and the head position lies between $0$ and $P$. Moreover, $ch'\le1$, the memory only
gains marked cells, and it is unchanged outside the cells $B_s+v$ for $v<K$. For every
$v<K$, if $M'$ marks cell $B_s+v$, then $M$ already marked that cell or the step oracle
accepts $(x,rr(S,\varphi),u,v)$; conversely, every $v$ with $V\le v<K$ accepted by the
step oracle has cell $B_s+v$ marked in $M'$. If $M'=M$, then $ch'=ch$, and if $M'\ne M$,
then $ch'=1$.
